nodes.label: District-Level Analysis of Child Malnutrition in India
nodes.rationale: Uses district-level evidence to evaluate roles of food, water, and healthcare simultaneously to avoid inefficient resource allocation by large programs like Jal Jeevan Mission and POSHAN 2.0.
nodes.norm_label: district-level analysis of child malnutrition in india

nodes.label: South Asian Enigma
nodes.rationale: Refers to the paradox where rapid economic growth has not eliminated widespread child malnutrition, linked to sanitation, female empowerment, and healthcare gaps.

nodes.label: Pathway 1: Food Availability
nodes.rationale: Proxied by district-level weighted crop yield to identify structural food insecurity independent of market access.

nodes.label: Pathway 2: Water and Sanitation
nodes.rationale: Focused on reducing enteric diseases that impair nutrient absorption even when food intake is adequate.

nodes.label: Pathway 3: Healthcare Reach
nodes.rationale: Includes antenatal care, immunisation, and women's education as a structural socioeconomic control influencing all pathways.

nodes.label: OLS Regression Model
nodes.rationale: Uses z-scored predictors (sanitation, education, deliveries, yield) to identify which structural factors drive the malnutrition index (R² = 0.523).

nodes.label: K-Means District Clustering
nodes.rationale: Groups 681 districts into 4 clusters using silhouette score and elbow method to identify structurally distinct policy target groups.

nodes.label: PCA Composite Malnutrition Index
nodes.rationale: Collapses four correlated outcomes (stunting, wasting, underweight, anaemia) into one policy-legible signal (PC1) capturing 59.8% shared variance.

nodes.label: Northeast India Structural Outlier
nodes.rationale: Isolated into Cluster 2 due to high sanitation but very low institutional deliveries, suggesting cultural or dietary diversity offsets formal healthcare gaps.
